NASB.1: For behold, the Lord GOD of hosts is going to remove from Jerusalem and Judah Both supply and support, the whole supply of bread And the whole supply of water;
NASB.2: The mighty man and the warrior, The judge and the prophet, The diviner and the elder,
NASB.3: The captain of fifty and the honorable man, The counselor and the expert artisan, And the skillful enchanter.
NASB.4: And I will make mere lads their princes, And capricious children will rule over them,
NASB.5: And the people will be oppressed, Each one by another, and each one by his neighbor; The youth will storm against the elder And the inferior against the honorable.
NASB.6: When a man lays hold of his brother in his father's house, [saying], 'You have a cloak, you shall be our ruler, And these ruins will be under your charge,'
NASB.7: He will protest on that day, saying, 'I will not be [your] healer, For in my house there is neither bread nor cloak; You should not appoint me ruler of the people.'
NASB.8: For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, Because their speech and their actions are against the LORD, To rebel against His glorious presence.
NASB.9: The expression of their faces bears witness against them, And they display their sin like Sodom; They do not [even] conceal [it]. Woe to them! For they have brought evil on themselves.
NASB.10: Say to the righteous that [it will go] well [with them], For they will eat the fruit of their actions.
NASB.11: Woe to the wicked! [It will go] badly [with him], For what he deserves will be done to him.
NASB.12: O My people! Their oppressors are children, And women rule over them. O My people! Those who guide you lead [you] astray And confuse the direction of your paths.
NASB.13: The LORD arises to contend, And stands to judge the people.
NASB.14: The LORD enters into judgment with the elders and princes of His people, 'It is you who have devoured the vineyard; The plunder of the poor is in your houses.
NASB.15: 'What do you mean by crushing My people And grinding the face of the poor?' Declares the Lord GOD of hosts.
NASB.16: Moreover, the LORD said, 'Because the daughters of Zion are proud And walk with heads held high and seductive eyes, And go along with mincing steps And tinkle the bangles on their feet,
NASB.17: Therefore the Lord will afflict the scalp of the daughters of Zion with scabs, And the LORD will make their foreheads bare.'
NASB.18: In that day the Lord will take away the beauty of [their] anklets, headbands, crescent ornaments,
NASB.20: headdresses, ankle chains, sashes, perfume boxes, amulets,
NASB.22: festal robes, outer tunics, cloaks, money purses,
NASB.23: hand mirrors, undergarments, turbans and veils.
NASB.24: Now it will come about that instead of sweet perfume there will be putrefaction; Instead of a belt, a rope; Instead of well-set hair, a plucked-out scalp; Instead of fine clothes, a donning of sackcloth; And branding instead of beauty.
NASB.25: Your men will fall by the sword And your mighty ones in battle.
NASB.26: And her gates will lament and mourn, And deserted she will sit on the ground.

NKJV.10: “Say to the righteous that it shall be well with them, For they shall eat the fruit of their doings.
NKJV.11: Woe to the wicked! It shall be ill with him, For the reward of his hands shall be given him.
NKJV.12: As for My people, children are their oppressors, And women rule over them. O My people! Those who lead you cause you to err, And destroy the way of your paths.”
NKJV.13: The LORD stands up to plead, And stands to judge the people.
NKJV.14: The LORD will enter into judgment With the elders of His people And His princes: “For you have eaten up the vineyard; The plunder of the poor is in your houses.

ESV.1: For behold, the Lord GOD of hosts is taking away from Jerusalem and from Judah support and supply,  all support of bread, and all support of water;
ESV.2: the mighty man and the soldier, the judge and the prophet, the diviner and the elder,
ESV.3: the captain of fifty and the man of rank, the counselor and the skillful magician and the expert in charms.
ESV.4: And I will make boys their princes, and infants  shall rule over them.
ESV.5: And the people will oppress one another, every one his fellow and every one his neighbor; the youth will be insolent to the elder, and the despised to the honorable.
ESV.6: For a man will take hold of his brother in the house of his father, saying: “You have a cloak; you shall be our leader, and this heap of ruins shall be under your rule”;
ESV.7: in that day he will speak out, saying: “I will not be a healer;  in my house there is neither bread nor cloak; you shall not make me leader of the people.”
ESV.8: For Jerusalem has stumbled, and Judah has fallen, because their speech and their deeds are against the LORD, defying his glorious presence.
ESV.9: For the look on their faces bears witness against them; they proclaim their sin like Sodom; they do not hide it. Woe to them! For they have brought evil on themselves.
ESV.10: Tell the righteous that it shall be well with them, for they shall eat the fruit of their deeds.
ESV.11: Woe to the wicked! It shall be ill with him, for what his hands have dealt out shall be done to him.
ESV.12: My people — infants are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, your guides mislead you and they have swallowed up  the course of your paths.
ESV.13: The LORD has taken his place to contend; he stands to judge peoples.
ESV.14: The LORD will enter into judgment with the elders and princes of his people: “It is you who have devoured  the vineyard, the spoil of the poor is in your houses.
ESV.15: What do you mean by crushing my people, by grinding the face of the poor?” declares the Lord GOD of hosts.
ESV.16: The LORD said: Because the daughters of Zion are haughty and walk with outstretched necks, glancing wantonly with their eyes, mincing along as they go, tinkling with their feet,
ESV.17: therefore the Lord will strike with a scab the heads of the daughters of Zion, and the LORD will lay bare their secret parts.
ESV.18: In that day the Lord will take away the finery of the anklets, the headbands, and the crescents;
ESV.19: the pendants, the bracelets, and the scarves;
ESV.20: the headdresses, the armlets, the sashes, the perfume boxes, and the amulets;
ESV.21: the signet rings and nose rings;
ESV.22: the festal robes, the mantles, the cloaks, and the handbags;
ESV.23: the mirrors, the linen garments, the turbans, and the veils.
ESV.24: Instead of perfume there will be rottenness; and instead of a belt, a rope; and instead of well-set hair, baldness; and instead of a rich robe, a skirt of sackcloth; and branding instead of beauty.
ESV.25: Your men shall fall by the sword and your mighty men in battle.
ESV.26: And her gates shall lament and mourn; empty, she shall sit on the ground.

NLT.1:
The Lord, the LORD of Heaven’s Armies,
will take away from Jerusalem and Judah
everything they depend on:
every bit of bread
and every drop of water,
NLT.2:
all their heroes and soldiers,
judges and prophets,
fortune-tellers and elders,
NLT.3:
army officers and high officials,
advisers, skilled sorcerers, and astrologers.
NLT.4:
I will make boys their leaders,
and toddlers their rulers.
NLT.5:
People will oppress each other —
man against man,
neighbor against neighbor.
Young people will insult their elders,
and vulgar people will sneer at the honorable.
NLT.6:
In those days a man will say to his brother,
“Since you have a coat, you be our leader!
Take charge of this heap of ruins!”
NLT.7:
But he will reply,
“No! I can’t help.
I don’t have any extra food or clothes.
Don’t put me in charge!”
NLT.8:
For Jerusalem will stumble,
and Judah will fall,
because they speak out against the LORD and refuse to obey him.
They provoke him to his face.
NLT.9:
The very look on their faces gives them away.
They display their sin like the people of Sodom
and don’t even try to hide it.
They are doomed!
They have brought destruction upon themselves.
NLT.10:
Tell the godly that all will be well for them.
They will enjoy the rich reward they have earned!
NLT.11:
But the wicked are doomed,
for they will get exactly what they deserve.
NLT.12:
Childish leaders oppress my people,
and women rule over them.
O my people, your leaders mislead you;
they send you down the wrong road.
NLT.13:
The LORD takes his place in court
and presents his case against his people.
NLT.14:
The LORD comes forward to pronounce judgment
on the elders and rulers of his people:
“You have ruined Israel, my vineyard.
Your houses are filled with things stolen from the poor.
NLT.15:
How dare you crush my people,
grinding the faces of the poor into the dust?”
demands the Lord, the LORD of Heaven’s Armies.
NLT.16:
The LORD says, “Beautiful Zion is haughty:
craning her elegant neck,
flirting with her eyes,
walking with dainty steps,
tinkling her ankle bracelets.
NLT.17:
So the Lord will send scabs on her head;
the LORD will make beautiful Zion bald.”
NLT.18:
On that day of judgment
the Lord will strip away everything that makes her beautiful:
ornaments, headbands, crescent necklaces,
NLT.20:
scarves, ankle bracelets, sashes,
perfumes, and charms;
NLT.22: party clothes, gowns, capes, and purses;
NLT.23:
mirrors, fine linen garments,
head ornaments, and shawls.
NLT.24:
Instead of smelling of sweet perfume, she will stink.
She will wear a rope for a sash,
and her elegant hair will fall out.
She will wear rough burlap instead of rich robes.
Shame will replace her beauty.
NLT.25:
The men of the city will be killed with the sword,
and her warriors will die in battle.
NLT.26:
The gates of Zion will weep and mourn.
The city will be like a ravaged woman,
huddled on the ground.

AMP.1:
Listen carefully, the Lord GOD of hosts is removing from Jerusalem and from Judah
Both supply and support, the whole supply of bread
And the whole supply of water;
AMP.2:
The brave man and the warrior [He is also removing],
The judge and the prophet,
The diviner and the elder,
AMP.3:
The captain of fifty and the man of honor,
The counselor and the expert artisan,
And the skillful enchanter.
AMP.4:
And I will make mere boys their princes,
And capricious (impulsive, unpredictable) children will rule over them.
AMP.5:
And the people will be oppressed,
Each one by another, and each one by his neighbor;
The boy will be arrogant and insolent toward the elder
And the vulgar (common) toward the honorable [person of rank].
AMP.6:
When a man takes hold of his brother in the house of his father, saying,
"You have a robe, you shall be our judge and ruler,
And this pile of ruins will be under your control,"
AMP.7:
He will protest on that day, saying,
"I will not be a governor;
For in my house there is neither bread nor clothing;
You should not make me a judge and ruler of the people."
AMP.8:
For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen,
Because their words and their actions are against the LORD,
To rebel against His glorious presence and defiantly provoke Him.
AMP.9:
Their partiality testifies against them,
They display their sin like Sodom;
They do not even hide it.
Woe (judgment is coming) to them!
For they have brought evil on themselves [as a reward].
AMP.10:
Say to the righteous that it will go well with them,
For they will eat the fruit of their [righteous] actions.
AMP.11:
Woe (judgment is coming) to the wicked! It shall go badly with him,
For what his hand has done shall be done to him.
AMP.12:
O My people! Children are their oppressors,
And women rule over them.
O My people! Your leaders lead you astray
And confuse (destroy, swallow up) the direction of your paths.
AMP.13:
The LORD rises to contend,
And stands to judge the people.
AMP.14:
The LORD enters into judgment with the elders of His people and their princes,
"For it is you who have devoured the vineyard [with your oppression, you have robbed the people and ruined the country];
The plunder of the poor is in your houses.
AMP.15:
"What do you mean by crushing My people
And grinding the face of the poor?"
Declares the Lord GOD of hosts.
AMP.16:
Moreover, the LORD said, "Because the daughters of Zion are proud
And walk with outstretched necks and seductive (flirtatious, alluring) eyes,
And trip along with mincing steps and an affected gait
And walk with jingling anklets on their feet,
AMP.17:
Therefore the Lord will afflict the crown of the head of the daughters of Zion with scabs [making them bald],
And the LORD will expose their foreheads (send them into captivity)."
AMP.18: In that day the Lord will take away the beauty of their anklets, [braided] caps, crescent [head] ornaments,
AMP.19: dangling earrings, bracelets, and the hanging veils and scarves,
AMP.20: head wraps (turbans), [short, jingling] ankle chains, sashes, perfume boxes, amulets (charms),
AMP.22: festival robes, outer tunics, shawls, handbags,
AMP.23: hand mirrors, [fine linen] undergarments, headbands, and veils [covering the entire body].
AMP.24:
Now it will come to pass that instead of the sweet fragrance of spices there will be [the stench of] rottenness;
Instead of a belt, a rope;
Instead of well-set hair, baldness;
Instead of fine clothes, a robe of sackcloth;
And branding [of captives by the scorching heat] instead of beauty.
AMP.25:
Your men will fall by the sword
And your mighty men in battle.
AMP.26:
And Jerusalem's gates will lament (cry out in grief) and mourn [as those who wail for the dead];
And she, being ruined and desolate, will sit upon the ground.

NET.1: Look, the sovereign LORD who commands armies is about to remove from Jerusalem and Judah every source of security, including all the food and water,
NET.2: the mighty men and warriors, judges and prophets, omen readers and leaders,
NET.3: captains of groups of fifty, the respected citizens, advisers and those skilled in magical arts, and those who know incantations.
NET.4: The LORD says, “I will make youths their officials; malicious young men will rule over them.
NET.5: The people will treat each other harshly; men will oppose each other; neighbors will fight. Youths will proudly defy the elderly and riffraff will challenge those who were once respected.
NET.6: Indeed, a man will grab his brother right in his father’s house and say, ‘You own a coat — you be our leader! This heap of ruins will be under your control.’
NET.7: At that time the brother will shout, ‘I am no doctor, I have no food or coat in my house; don’t make me a leader of the people!’”
NET.8: Jerusalem certainly stumbles, Judah falls, for their words and their actions offend the LORD; they rebel against his royal authority.
NET.9: The look on their faces testifies to their guilt; like the people of Sodom they openly boast of their sin. Too bad for them! For they bring disaster on themselves.
NET.10: Tell the innocent it will go well with them, for they will be rewarded for what they have done.
NET.11: Too bad for the wicked sinners! For they will get exactly what they deserve.
NET.12: Oppressors treat my people cruelly; creditors rule over them. My people’s leaders mislead them; they give you confusing directions.
NET.13: The LORD takes his position to judge; he stands up to pass sentence on his people.
NET.14: The LORD comes to pronounce judgment on the leaders of his people and their officials. He says, “It is you who have ruined the vineyard! You have stashed in your houses what you have stolen from the poor.
NET.15: Why do you crush my people and grind the faces of the poor?” The sovereign LORD who commands armies has spoken.
NET.16: The LORD says, “The women of Zion are proud. They walk with their heads high and flirt with their eyes. They skip along and the jewelry on their ankles jingles.
NET.17: So the sovereign master will afflict the foreheads of Zion’s women with skin diseases, the LORD will make the front of their heads bald.”
NET.18: At that time the sovereign master will remove their beautiful ankle jewelry, neck ornaments, crescent shaped ornaments,
NET.20: headdresses, ankle ornaments, sashes, sachets, amulets,
NET.23: garments, vests, head coverings, and gowns.
NET.24: A putrid stench will replace the smell of spices, a rope will replace a belt, baldness will replace braided locks of hair, a sackcloth garment will replace a fine robe, and a prisoner’s brand will replace beauty.
NET.25: Your men will fall by the sword, your strong men will die in battle.
NET.26: Her gates will mourn and lament; deprived of her people, she will sit on the ground.
